title: Dutch East India Company (VOC)
summary: On 20 March 1602 the States-General of the Dutch Republic chartered the VOC, uniting six companies and granting a 21-year trade monopoly east of the Cape of Good Hope. Batavia (present-day Jakarta) became its headquarters and main administrative centre in 1619, and the government formally dissolved the company on 31 December 1799.

uncertainty.note: Chartered 20 March 1602; formally dissolved 31 December 1799 per World History Encyclopedia (Encyclopedia.com does not give a dissolution date).

as_recorded.value: the government formally dissolved the VOC on December 31, 1799

where.modern_name: Jakarta, Indonesia (site of Batavia, the VOC headquarters from 1619)
where.historical_name: Batavia (Jaccatra, conquered 1619), headquarters of the VOC; the company was chartered by the States-General of the Dutch Republic

importance.justification: Chartered monopoly company that ran Dutch trade in Asia for nearly two centuries.

reviewer_note: Least sure: the point is Batavia (HQ from 1619), not the place of chartering, since no opened page names the city where the States-General sat. Banda massacre (1621) is on the World History page but omitted. Charter described as covering Asia (WHE) and east of the Cape of Good Hope (Encyclopedia.com).
